title: Inspiration4 crew urine inflammation proteins, NULISA-seq (OSD-656) - no urine chemistry

source.name: OSD-656: SpaceX Inspiration4 Urine Inflammation Panel (Multiplex, NULISAseq)
source.license: not stated in the OSDR API response; the files are publicly released (OSDR file records 'restricted': false). Check the OSDR study page before reuse.
source.citation: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR). OSD-656: SpaceX Inspiration4 Urine Inflammation Panel (Multiplex, NULISAseq). Study version 2, submitted 2023-08-31, publicly released 2024-05-14. https://osdr.nasa.gov/bio/repo/data/studies/OSD-656 (no dataset DOI is stated in the OSDR metadata). Investigators listed by OSDR: Eliah Overbey (co-investigator); Christopher Mason (principal investigator). Publications listed by OSDR: The Space Omics and Medical Atlas (SOMA) and international astronaut biobank (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07639-y); Collection of Biospecimens from the Inspiration4 Mission Establishes the Standards for the Space Omics and Medical Atlas (SOMA) (doi:10.1038/s41467-024-48806-z).

caveats: Inspiration4 was a ~3-day civilian low-Earth-orbit flight (OSDR metadata: mission 2021-09-16 to 2021-09-18) with n=4 crew. These files contain NO in-flight samples: only pre-flight L-92/L-44/L-3 and post-flight R+1/R+45/R+82 (the OSDR study description says 'The crew collected biospecimen samples before, during, and after flight', but no in-flight sample is in these files). These files provide a real post-flight recovery shape only (no reference ranges exist in these files); they are NOT a model of a long-duration exploration mission and must not be presented as one.

within_own_range is an OBSERVATION (value inside the reference range the laboratory printed for that same sample, bounds inclusive; one-sided ranges compare one bound), not an alert, not a diagnosis and not a NASA threshold. NASA publishes no numeric in-flight alert threshold for these analytes.
Timepoint dates are nominal and derived (label offset from the OSDR mission start for L-, from the mission end for R+); actual collection timestamps are not in these files.

OSD-656 is a urine INFLAMMATION-PROTEIN panel (NULISA-seq), not a urinalysis: there is NO urinary calcium, volume, pH, oxalate, citrate or creatinine. It cannot feed the bone -> renal-stone / hydration case; that case needs crew-entered urine volume, not this file.

Unit NPQ = NULISA Protein Quantification: log2 of IPC-normalised sequencing counts (definition quoted from the OSDR assay metadata). Relative units: compare a target only with itself (within a subject over time); not a concentration, no reference range.
Urine was collected at 6 timepoints (no R+194). Samples absent from BOTH the submitted and the TRANSFORMED file: C001 L-3, C001 R+1.

Values come from the OSDR 'Original Submitted' laboratory sheet (LSDS-64_Multiplex_urine.immune.AlamarPanel_SUBMITTED.xlsx); every value was cross-checked against the ALSDA TRANSFORMED CSV (4444 values, 0 disagreements).
The 'Percent_normalized_value' / '<target>_percent_normalized_value' columns are not included (normalisation basis not documented in the files fetched).

Size budget: NPQ values are rounded half-to-even to 3 decimals (published with up to 15-17 significant digits); 0.001 log2 units is a ~0.07% relative change. The sha256 of each source file is in data.study.files for exact verification.

Exact-zero NPQ values (133 values in 27 targets) are reproduced as published. The files fetched state no limit of detection, and no NPQ below 0 occurs, so 0 is the floor of this log2-count scale: show it as 'at assay floor / not detected', not as a level, and do not use it as a baseline for change scores. Per target (zeros/samples): AGER 2/22, BDNF 17/22, C1QA 22/22, CCL16 1/22, CCL17 1/22, CCL22 2/22, CCL23 8/22, CCL28 3/22, CD200 2/22, CXCL13 9/22, CXCL2 1/22, FASLG 2/22, FGF19 7/22, IL12RB1 2/22, IL17B 1/22, IL17C 13/22, IL18 1/22, IL1RL1 2/22, IRAK4 9/22, KDR 9/22, MMP10 1/22, MMP3 1/22, TNFSF10 1/22, TNFSF15 3/22, TNFSF8 6/22, VCAM1 6/22, WNT16 1/22.

ALSDA TRANSFORMED CSV header defects (the TRANSFORMED file is used only as a cross-check): 2 blank header cell(s) at column index [2, 214]; those columns are not used. 'il1rl1': the TRANSFORMED file has a 'il1rl1_percent_normalized_value' header but no 'il1rl1_concentration_npq' header (header misalignment next to a blank column); its NPQ is never read from the TRANSFORMED file. il1rl1: the TRANSFORMED column headed 'il1rl1_percent_normalized_value' equals the submitted IL1RL1 NPQ in 22/22 samples, so that header is mislabelled; IL1RL1 values here come from the Original Submitted file.
